entries.title: Identical xxxx sequence in three contexts: responsive units
entries.question: Does the P4 − P3 response to the identical xxxx sequence differ between the main, randomized and sequenced contexts?
entries.relation_to_published: Uses DANDI 000253, the data of PMC11741236. The paper and its Extended Data show no xxxx comparison across main, randomized and sequenced contexts and no context decoding (PUBLISHED_VS_PROPOSED.md).

figures.caption: Contrasts C1–C4 and drift D per area: mean over mice of the per-mouse median over responsive units.
figures.uncertainty: 95 % percentile bootstrap over mice (10,000 draws, seed 20261012)

entries.result: No contrast passes the preregistered test in any of 20 tested area × contrast cells (exact sign-flip over mice, BH; smallest p 0.090, smallest q 0.81). VISam not tested (5 mice).
entries.interpretation: Every contrast is not distinguishable from zero at this resolution. Bootstrap CIs lie within about ±1 Hz in VISp, VISl and VISal and reach about 1.7 Hz in VISrl and 1.38 Hz in VISpm; this is not an equivalence test. The drift contrast is of the same size, so no context effect is identified either way.
limitations: Responsiveness was decided on P1 (always x), so the population is x-selected; C4 (yyyy) is measured in units chosen for x.
Context is confounded with time and state (block order fixed, running speed differs between contexts).
With 8 and 7 mice, VISrl and VISpm reach q < 0.05 only if 3 or 6 other cells reject first.
The spike–stimulus clock check is not independent of the stimulus table.
Session 1186358749 follows a different block design and is excluded.

replications.scope: every confirmatory cell, recomputed from the NWB files
replications.note: 288 of 297 checks match; the 7 mismatches were statements in the write-up, since corrected

entries.title: Identical xxxx sequence in three contexts: all quality units (selection check)
entries.question: Does the responsiveness filter change the showcase 1 result?
entries.relation_to_published: Uses DANDI 000253, the data of PMC11741236. The paper and its Extended Data show no xxxx comparison across main, randomized and sequenced contexts and no context decoding (PUBLISHED_VS_PROPOSED.md).

figures.caption: As the primary figure, over all quality units in visual areas (post hoc).
figures.uncertainty: 95 % percentile bootstrap over mice (10,000 draws, one generator seeded 20261012, consumed in table order)

entries.result: No cell passes q < 0.05 among 24 cells (smallest p 0.017, smallest q 0.28); CI bounds lie within ±0.7 Hz.
entries.interpretation: The responsiveness filter does not change the conclusion; not an equivalence test.
limitations: CI bounds depend on the bootstrap seed and cell order (VISpm C2 lower bound 0.013–0.017 across seeds).
Independent check reproduced the C2 cells only.

replications.note: the other contrasts were not rerun

entries.title: Decoding context from the identical xxxx response (preregistered version 2)
entries.question: Is main 2 vs sequenced context decodable from responses to the identical xxxx sequence, above the majority baseline and beyond linear drift, and more at P4 than at P3?
entries.relation_to_published: Uses DANDI 000253, the data of PMC11741236. The paper and its Extended Data show no xxxx comparison across main, randomized and sequenced contexts and no context decoding (PUBLISHED_VS_PROPOSED.md).

figures.caption: Linear-SVM accuracy minus the majority baseline at P4 and P3, and A_P4 − A_P3, per area; features residualised on block position.
figures.controls: majority baseline on the same folds; block-position covariate
figures.uncertainty: 95 % percentile bootstrap over mice (10,000 draws, seed 20261012)

entries.result: No area decodes context above the majority baseline at P4 or P3 (smallest q 0.18; 10 of 12 means negative), and no P4 − P3 gain (smallest q 0.28). AUC 0.46–0.63.
entries.interpretation: With linear block-position drift removed, context is not decodable above the majority baseline; a context effect that ramps linearly with block position would be removed with the drift.
limitations: The sequenced blocks all precede the main-2 blocks, so the adjustment removes any context difference a linear trend explains.
The VISal nominal P4 − P3 gain (p 0.047, q 0.28) depends on the seed: at seed 20261013 it is −0.015 (p 0.51).

replications.scope: decoding in all six areas; per-session scores, family means and p
replications.note: 0 of 11 fields per area differ by more than 1e-6

replications.scope: the same decoding at a second seed, all six areas
replications.note: no cell reaches p < 0.13; the VISal gain is −0.015 (p 0.51) against +0.042 (p 0.047)

entries.title: LFP clock offset of two replaced-version probe files
entries.question: Is the stored-seconds LFP time axis of 000253 0.240923.1441 aligned to the spike clock within one sample (0.8 ms)?
entries.relation_to_published: Data check for a proposed LFP showcase; the paper reports no such check.

figures.caption: Median spike-triggered LFP trough lag over units, early and late 70-s windows; bars span the units' range.
figures.controls: independent check recovers a 5.0 ms spike-time shift at 4.95–4.97 ms

entries.result: Probe 1 of 1232959154: -10.03 ms early and -10.20 ms late, constant over the session (independent check −9.73 and −9.76 ms). Probe 1 of 1203581890: within 0.8 ms (-0.26 and -0.33 ms; independent check +0.24 and +0.28 ms).
entries.interpretation: Stored seconds are within one sample in one probe and offset by a constant about 10 ms in the other, so each probe needs this check before band power.
limitations: The delay from a spike to its LFP-band trough cannot be separated from the clock offset.
17–21 % of units have a positive-dominant STA (independent check).
Two probes reproduced; four others tested remotely remain unverified; the remote reads went beyond the Gate B authorisation.
The 1203581890 probe file was not replaced between versions.

replications.scope: both probes, early and late windows, from the downloaded files
replications.note: −9.73 and −9.76 ms in 1232959154; +0.24 and +0.28 ms in 1203581890; each within one sample (0.8 ms) of the showcase value
